title: Third reason: every natural faculty has its natural perfection, and for the moral faculties that is righteousness
source_text: LIV. Nec etiam est ulla naturalis facultas cui sua perfectio naturalis non respondeat. Morales autem facultates, ratione quarum homo est virtutis & vitii capax, homini naturales sunt, non minus quam caeterae. Qua in re autem earum naturalis perfectio consistere potest, nisi in ipsa justitia & sanctitate, de qua jam quaestio est?
pass_a_gloss: Nor also is there any natural faculty to which its natural perfection does not correspond. But the moral faculties, by reason of which man is capable of virtue and vice, are natural to man, no less than the others. But in what can their natural perfection consist, except in that very justice and sanctity, about which the question now is?
pass_b_english: Again, there is no natural faculty without a natural perfection that belongs to it. Man's moral faculties, which make him capable of virtue and vice, are as natural to him as his other faculties. What can their natural perfection be, if not the very righteousness and holiness now in question?

choices.why: Kept literal; the pair defines the moral faculties.
